conviction_note: Two offsetting pieces: a genuinely unpriced positive read-through from Ambarella's largest LTA partner Hanwha Vision (record security quarter, AI-camera mix 46%->59%, disclosed in Korean on 2026-08-06) worth about +2.5, netted against the discovery that the baseline's -20% 20-day run-up is entirely the round-trip of the 30-31 July NXP takeover-rumour pop rather than a fundamental de-rate, which removes the 'washed-out, low bar' premise a reader would otherwise take from the baseline (about -1.0); I shaded the sum down slightly for this name's habit of falling on prints (5 of 7).

findings.finding: Hanwha Vision - which signed an $800m+, 10-year, multi-generation edge-AI SoC LTA with Ambarella on 2026-05-28 - reported its security segment's best quarter ever for calendar Q2 2026 (KRW 394.6bn, +20.1% YoY vs KRW 328.4bn), with AI-CCTV rising to 59% of network-camera revenue from 46% a year earlier; that AI mix shift is exactly the content-per-camera driver behind Ambarella's professional IoT line, which is ~75% of its revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a Korean-language disclosure by a KRX-listed company (Hanwha Vision, 489790) published 2026-08-06. Every US-facing AMBA preview I could find is anchored on the same three numbers - consensus revenue $107.76m, non-GAAP EPS ~$0.17, and the unchanged FY27 'we're still thinking 10-15%' - and none of them mentions Hanwha Vision's own quarter. If this had been priced, you would see (a) at least one AMBA note in the four weeks after 6 August citing professional-security demand, and (b) some fundamental re-rating in the tape; instead AMBA simply retraced the takeover-rumour pop and now sits 5.4% below its last undisturbed close, i.e. the market did no fundamental work at all in that window. The $800m LTA headline itself IS priced - it was released alongside the Q1 print on 2026-05-28 and the stock still fell 21% - but the partner's subsequent operating performance is not.
findings.independence: Arashi Vision (Insta360, 688775.SH), whose Ace/Ace Pro line runs Ambarella firmware, filed H1 2026 on 2026-08-27: revenue RMB5.52bn, +50.29% YoY, consumer smart imaging devices RMB4.788bn, +51.56% - a different downstream camera maker, different exchange, different language, pointing the same way on unit demand through Ambarella's May-July quarter. https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-08-28/doc-inipvmnh0281602.shtml . Caveat that keeps this genuinely secondary: the Ambarella-Insta360 link rests on firmware evidence (https://www.goprawn.com/forum/ambarella-cams/20635-insta360-ace-and-ace-pro-firmware-hacks) not a disclosure, and Insta360's new flagship X6 launched 2026-08-12 is described as using a 4nm 'custom chip' with no vendor named (https://petapixel.com/2026/08/12/insta360-wants-its-flagship-x6-to-be-way-more-than-a-360-degree-camera/), which if it is not Ambarella cuts the other way from Q3 onward. I am not filing that as a separate finding because it is the same entity read in the opposite direction.

findings.finding: The baseline's -20.07% 20-day run-up is not a fundamental de-rate: AMBA closed $69.19 on 2026-07-29, jumped +7.08% to $74.09 on 30 July and +16.08% to $86.00 on 31 July on the FT report of NXP takeover talks, and has since bled straight back to $65.43 - only 5.4% below the last undisturbed pre-rumour close, against SMH -6.6% from 7 August to 3 September. There has been no report anywhere that the NXP process ended.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a correction to how the sealed baseline reads rather than new news, and it has two offsetting legs that I am deliberately filing as one because they rest on a single fact - the July NXP rumour. Leg one (negative, dominant): a -20% 20-day run-up, -31.5% from the 52-week high and a 2.14 put/call open-interest ratio normally say 'expectations already cut, positioning defensive, bar low'. Here none of that is true - the drawdown is a mechanical premium unwind concentrated in the six sessions after 7 August, the pre-rumour price is essentially intact beta-adjusted, and the put-heavy open interest is more plausibly deal-related option residue than a fundamental bearish bet. So the standard 'beaten-down semi bounces on an in-line print' trade is not actually set up, and anyone sizing off the baseline's run-up field will over-weight it. Leg two (positive, smaller): the market is now pricing deal probability at roughly zero even though no source reports the talks dead, leaving a live low-probability, high-payoff tail - a signed merger agreement released alongside earnings, which does happen. If the market still carried any deal probability, the stock would not have round-tripped below the undisturbed close; if it were confident the talks were dead, there would be a story saying so, and there is not.
findings.independence: The rumour date, the +16% move and the fact the talks were unresolved are independently documented at https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ambarella-reportedly-in-talks-to-be-acquired-by-nxp-semiconductors-shares-spike-4829078 (2026-07-31). The SMH comparison comes from a separate price series, https://stockanalysis.com/etf/smh/history/ (Aug 7 $582.70 -> Sep 3 $544.39). My AMBA series reconciles exactly to the sealed baseline (65.425/81.85-1 = -20.07%, the baseline's own 20-day figure), so this is not a data disagreement, it is a reading of the same data.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider transactions: no Form 4 or Form 144 since 2026-07-10, which looked like a merger blackout until I checked the prior year - Ambarella also filed nothing between 2025-06-27 and 2025-09-04, so the gap is the normal RSU vest cadence, not a signal (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001280263.json)

The three SCHEDULE 13G filings clustered 2026-07-31, 08-07 and 08-14 turned out to be Vanguard (5.01%), State Street (5.8%) and T. Rowe Price (5.9%) crossing the threshold - passive/index, not event-driven arbitrageurs

The 8-K filed 2026-07-01 with an Item 5.02 tag is only the annual-meeting director elections and the amended 2021 equity plan; no officer departure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001280263/000119312526292824/d139114d8k.htm)
No report from any source that the NXP-Ambarella talks were abandoned, and no AMBA-specific downgrade or estimate cut that would explain the August slide beyond the rumour unwind

The 25% Section 232 semiconductor tariff took effect 2026-01-15, i.e. before the quarter being reported, and the 6 August 2026 Section 232 action was polysilicon/solar, not logic - nothing new landed inside the May-July window (https://globaltaxnews.ey.com/news/2026-0209-us-section-232-proclamation-imposes-25-percent-tariff-on-certain-semiconductors)

The large Q1 inventory build (from $52.2m at 31 Jan to $80.4m at 30 Apr, days 99 -> 145) is real but was in the 30 April 10-Q and was explained on the 28 May call as deliberate supply securing, so it has been public for three months and is priced (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001280263/000119312526253198/amba-20260430.htm)

The July 2026 collapse from $88.34 to $61.84 was the broad semiconductor selloff (SMH down almost 9% over the period), not AMBA-specific news (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514666-why-ambarella-inc8217s-amba-stock-is-down-676)
WT Microelectronics is the only >10% channel at 60.7% of Q1 revenue, but it is a ~$40bn Taiwanese distributor and its monthly revenue disclosures carry no attributable Ambarella signal
Ambarella's own careers/job-board footprint (~22 US openings, mostly physical-design and interns) shows neither a team addition nor a hiring freeze big enough to read anything from
Could not source a foundry/wafer price-increase datapoint specific enough to size the gross-margin risk against the guided 59.0-60.5%
baseline_tension: My positive finding cuts against the put-heavy open interest and against this name's 5-of-7 negative reaction history, while my second finding cuts against the baseline's own run-up field by showing the -20% is a takeover-rumour round-trip rather than the capitulation it looks like - so the net is a small positive that explicitly refuses both the bearish skew read and the naive 'oversold bounce' read.
